items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: In fact, to be truthful, I liked Don better than I did Coleman Hawkins.

ctx.x: Well, did he have power, when you first heard him

Yeah, yeah. But then when he got to New York, he got more finesse and started to playing fluid and legnit, you know, making pretty sounds, but with things that he played, was something else. In fact, to be truthful, I liked Don better than I did Coleman Hawkins. Because Don went as far as to join Coleman Hawkins, to analyze what he was doing and put with what he would do as well and he

was playing a lot then, you know, to be doing the things I tell you he was doing. And he had an occassion at Kelley's Stables where Hawk was appearing. He played two shows nightly. 12 and 2; the clubs ran until four o'clock in New York at that time. And Don was in the band. And well when Hawk would be getting to work, the place would be packed. People would be sitting there with the assumption that they were listening to Coleman Hawkins, when they was listening to Don.
